cells.tense: You are tracking what is arriving and turning it into a route someone else can follow.
cells.ask: Take one thing you can do well, walk one person through it, put them in charge of the next step, and stay quiet while they try.
cells.core:
What's arriving, you're reading as a shape, not a mood. You see what's about to matter and put it in order before it lands. That's discipline doing its work — the mind working out a route and handing it to whoever can't read the water yet.

This is a steady place to stand. It holds when your sense of the way stops being only yours and becomes something you can pass across a table. Keeping it costs you something: a route is only worth anything if you keep working out new ones. That cost is the point. What you say plainly, they can carry without you.

cells.tense: You are already navigating a passage that has not opened yet, and you are steering hard.
cells.ask: Pick the outcome you have run through your head most this week, do one real thing toward it today, and then leave it alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're standing at the entrance doing the work before anything has arrived. Every version of what's coming is already mapped out in your head, corrected and said twice — and none of it has happened yet. The bracing feels like discipline. It isn't. It's the same read running past anything solid to read.

What you're steering toward can't be steered from this side. Things start when they start, and you spend the waiting drawing rooms you're not standing in. Put the pencil down for one stretch. Not because the read is wrong — because it needs something real in front of it to be worth anything.

cells.tense: You had something worth handing over and you are still standing at the door you already walked past.
cells.ask: Call one person who could use what you know and offer it plainly, without waiting to be asked.
cells.core:
You can feel it when the subject comes up — your read on where things need to go. What stalled was the passing of it. Somewhere the offering started to feel unsafe, or too late, or not worth saying, so the route stayed private. You've been standing behind that door and it moved on without you.

The read didn't leave. It just hasn't had an opening to run through. What brings it back isn't one more push at the threshold; it's touching why it matters what direction another person gets. That comes back through the people themselves, not through more thinking about them.

cells.tense: You are working out the passage right now and filing it under anything but your own name.
cells.ask: Name one thing you saw clearly before anyone else did this week and say out loud that you were the one who saw it.
cells.core:
The read is already working. You catch what's coming, you say where things need to go before the room does, and the room follows you on it — and you call that the mood of the room, or the obvious next step, or what anyone would have said. The route is being drawn. Your name isn't on it.

This isn't modesty. It's a habit of crediting the situation instead of yourself, and it stops you building anything on what you actually see. Take one clear read you've made and put your name on it. Not the whole thing — one line, said plainly, as if you were sure it was yours.

attempts.check: The record does not support any claim that the person feels lost, is actually lost, or has been given bad directions by anyone; it also does not license me to say what has failed in the guidance — only that the capacity to chart and pass on a passage is running. A reader could reasonably object that they are not a guide at all, that no one follows them, but the ask does not need them to be a guide in title, only to name publicly what they would say if someone asked for the way; if my read is wrong, the ask still gives them a concrete test of how clearly they can make their knowing cross to another person, and the sentence that serves me more than them was any line implying they have been a failure to others.
